title: Roll out catalogue fix to live runners and purge test entries
goal:
Roll out catalogue fix to live runners and purge test entries
Source: docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/RESPONSE.md WP-F (runbook) + section 6 end-to-end verification, RESPONSE_SURVEY.md q23/q24. Parent bug: task b3401f19.

This is the ONLY package that touches live runners/engine state. Requires explicit human permission. Blocked by WP-A, WP-B, WP-C merged and deployed (backend image rebuilt) and WP-E merged (so cleanup is not re-polluted); WP-D preferred but not required.

Runbook: (1) Install local runners from the RUNNER BUNDLE into a dedicated directory (e.g. ~/.kainbain/runner-install/<runnerId>/ via runner/updates) -- do NOT run them from /home/server/projects/kainbain/runner (RESPONSE.md N1: engine checkout switched between branches replaced daemon.js 4s after boot). Update service definitions/launch scripts for local-alpha, local-bravo (and any local-*). (2) Edit ~/.kainbain/runner-local-*.env: REMOVE KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS (recommended, discovery becomes source of truth) or reduce to harness-qualified ids only. (3) Fix server2-alpha install so the pi leg dependency resolves (reinstall from post-WP-B bundle); check Muse MSP provider config (MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY). (4) Restart runners; trigger requestModelRediscovery from Settings. (5) Purge pollution via WP-C admin DELETE: muse::meta::test-fleet-model; quarantined bare/provider ids removable or left for audit; revoked runner test-fleet-muse may stay revoked or be deleted via existing runner API. (6) Verify per RESPONSE.md section 6: section 3.1 shows discovered/pinned+discovered + per-harness ok:true (never {}), versions.build.sha matches deployed commit, codeChangedSinceBoot false; section 3.2 shows no bare/provider entries, no test-fleet-model, every entry harnesses length 1; UI Muse picker shows "N runners" harness badge, muse-ember with "N runners", no gemma4/deepseek/test-fleet-model, dropped models grey "0 runners" with Remove permanently; regression: removed-from-leg model stays at "0 runners", admin DELETE removes it, re-advertise brings it back; npm test for runner/, api/flow/dispatch/, api/routes/projects.*, fleetModelOptions, ModelSelector.test.jsx; WP-E guard proves no suite touched ~/.kainbain/engine.

Survey constraints: q23 user pre-approved ONLY "removing test or dummy catalogue entries" -- "I would say restarting local runners but that would likely cause task agents to kill themselves so maybe not but maybe recommend to user to do". So: agent must RECOMMEND runner restarts to the user/operator, never execute them itself. q24 overall approach approved.

Acceptance: all section-6 checks pass; live state contains zero test-fleet entries. Sequencing: BLOCKED BY WP-A + WP-B + WP-C + WP-E; gates WP-G.

#!/bin/bash
# Thin shim: the full-project verification gate lives in
# scripts/run-tests.mjs (cross-platform, `npm test` is canonical). Kept so
# `deploy.sh --prod` and older docs/paths keep working.

exec node scripts/run-tests.mjs "$@"

---
#!/usr/bin/env node
/***
 * MARK: run-tests.mjs
 * @description Cross-platform full-project verification gate: the same seven
 *   checks the old `run-tests.sh` ran plus the Container Tests branch, the
 *   Frontend Build branch (exercises the deprecation gate), the Dependency
 *   Audit Gate, the Proof Hygiene branch, and the Binary Guard branch, in a
 *   single overlap window
 *   (the two unit suites
 *   alone take ~2x35s sequentially, so overlapping keeps the wall near one
 *   suite), with identical `Running <name>... PASS/FAIL (<s>s)` lines and exit semantics —
 *   but driven by Node (`node:child_process`, no shell), so it runs on
 *   Linux, macOS, and Windows with only Node + npm installed. Shells out
 *   only to `npm`/Node/Docker; the two environment-conditional branches
 *   report SKIP instead of failing when their runtime is absent (Security
 *   Script Tests without `bash`, Container Tests without a Docker daemon).
 *   The fast branches share one overlap window; the Canary Tests branch runs
 *   alone afterwards (see splitGatePhases) — same suites, same exit
 *   semantics, but the heaviest branch never shares CPUs with the unit
 *   suites. Fail-fast is ON by default (see resolveFailFast): when the fast
 *   phase fails, the gate writes its verdict (`verdict.json` plus one

1|# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — WP-F: Roll out catalogue fix to live runners and purge test entries
2|
3|Task: `8c7e2d15-3f17-41a1-b905-99ca5e536c83` · Parent bug: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`
4|Source: `docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/RESPONSE.md` WP-F runbook (§4) + §6 end-to-end verification, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23/q24, `TICKETS.md` sequencing.

7|
8|## Goal
9|
10|Bring the live fleet onto the fixed catalogue stack (WP-A + WP-B + WP-C deployed, WP-E merged) and purge test pollution from live engine state, leaving zero `test-fleet` entries and a catalogue that satisfies RESPONSE.md §6 — without the agent ever touching a running task runner itself.
11|
12|## Success Criteria
13|
14|1. Gates honoured: WP-A, WP-B, WP-C merged and deployed (backend image rebuilt to a recorded commit), WP-E merged; WP-D status recorded (preferred, not blocking); explicit human permission recorded before any live-state step.
15|2. Agent performed only pre-approved live actions: read-only checks + DELETE of test/dummy catalogue entries via the WP-C admin route. All runner reinstall / env-edit / restart steps were executed by the human operator from agent-provided instructions (never by the agent).
16|3. RESPONSE.md §6 passes end to end: §3.1 shows `discovered`/`pinned+discovered` + per-harness `ok:true`, `versions.build.sha` matches deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot: false`; §3.2 shows no `bare`/`provider` entries, no `test-fleet-model`, every entry `harnesses.length === 1`; UI checks pass; regression check passes; named `npm test` suites pass; WP-E guard proves no suite touched `~/.kainbain/engine`.
17|4. Live state contains zero `test-fleet` entries: `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` gone from `fleet-catalog.json`; revoked runner `test-fleet-muse` left revoked for audit (survey q4 asks delete-completely, but no runner-record DELETE endpoint exists — operator explicitly accepts the infeasibility or removes it out-of-band).
18|5. Execution evidence is recorded in this task's docs folder (gate record, operator handoff receipts, verification log) so WP-G can be decision-gated on it.
19|
20|## Approach
21|
22|"Make change easy, then make the change": the agent does all of the safe, reversible preparation itself (Phases 0–1: gate checks, read-only rehearsal, exact operator commands, backups, dry-run verification scripts), then hands precisely two execution bundles to the operator (Phases 2–3: reinstall/env/restart — recommended, never executed by the agent), then performs only the pre-approved purge itself (Phase 4), then verifies everything against §6 (Phase 5) and records the evidence WP-G needs (Phase 6).
23|
24|Big/risky items come first: permission + gate verification and the self-kill-safe restart sequencing are resolved before any live state is touched; the irreversible DELETE comes only after WP-E-merged is proven (no re-pollution) and backups exist.
25|
26|### Survey mapping (binding constraints)
27|
28|Parent survey (`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`):
29|
30|- q23: user pre-approved ONLY "Removing test or dummy catalogue entries". Note: "restarting local runners … would likely cause task agents to kill themselves so maybe not but maybe recommend to user to do" → agent RECOMMENDS restarts, never executes them.
31|- q24: overall structural approach approved.
32|- Carried context: q1 keep 0-runner entries indefinitely + "Remove permanently" action; q3/q4 unverified = 0 runners, selectable but marked; q7 block non-canonical ids; q8 harness-qualified ids; q15 warn-only on version mismatch (block only on real incompatibility).
33|
34|This task's `SURVEY.md` (q1–q6, answers RECORDED — actuals below, superseding the plan-time Recommended-default assumptions):
35|
36|| # | Question | Actual answer |
37||---|---|---|
38|| q1 | Agent restarting runners? | Agent suggests, operator executes (Recommended) — notes: "The main worry is that they kill themselves while executing a task if we can avoid that it's safer to execute" |
39|| q2 | Cleanup timing? | As soon as WP-A/B/C deployed + WP-E merged (Recommended) |
40|| q3 | What to delete? | Test entries PLUS old leftover entries that no runner provides (NOT the Recommended test/dummy-only) |
41|| q4 | Revoked `test-fleet-muse` runner? | Delete it completely (NOT the Recommended leave-revoked) |
42|| q5 | `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` pin list? | Remove it; discovery is source of truth (Recommended) |
43|| q6 | On any failed check? | Stop immediately and report (Recommended) |
44|
45|Binding-constraint reconciliation (agent execution scope):
46|
47|- q3 vs parent q23: parent `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23 pre-approved ONLY "removing test or dummy catalogue entries" for agent execution. The broader q3 "test-plus-leftover" scope therefore needs a FRESH explicit human grant (who/when/exact ids) before the agent may DELETE any quarantined leftover. Until that grant exists, agent DELETEs stay test/dummy-only and quarantined leftovers are left for audit (Phase 4 step 17 default stands).

"Delete completely" cannot be executed by the agent through any API; the revoked `test-fleet-muse` record stays for audit unless the operator removes it out-of-band. The operator must explicitly accept this infeasibility (or perform the removal themselves) — it must not be silently treated as done.

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash
   bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard
   ```

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash
bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore <recovery-ref>
```

Restore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real
index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could
not save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.

## Always fine

Read-only inspection such as `status`, `log`, `show`, `diff`, `blame`,
`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.
Staging named files to inspect `diff --cached`, and a temporary stash around a
tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

## The rest

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.
- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing
  source-control trees.
- Do not create or edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` to hide the user's
  files, and do not stash the user's files (including `stash push -u`) to make
  `git status` look clean. "Leave the working tree clean", "tidy up", and
  similar phrasing do not authorize committing, pushing, ignoring, excluding,
  stashing, or deleting the user's files; clean up only scratch you created
  and say the user's files remain.
- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.
- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

## Locks and corrupt state

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

Never commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot
explain.

## If you already made an unwanted write

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.


index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could
not save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.

`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.

tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

explain.

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE

usage() {
  echo "usage: workspace-recovery.sh save [label] | restore <recovery-ref>" >&2
  exit 2
}

die() {
  echo "workspace recovery: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "git is unavailable"
root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "not an ordinary Git workspace"
head=$(git -C "$root" rev-parse --verify HEAD 2>/dev/null) || die "unborn HEAD is unsupported"
[ -z "$(git -C "$root" ls-files -u)" ] || die "an unmerged index is unsupported"
saved_ref=

write_recovery_commit() {
  local message=$1 tree=$2
  shift 2
  printf '%s\n' "$message" |
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="TBH Recovery" \
    GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="recovery@localhost" \
    GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="TBH Recovery" \
    GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="recovery@localhost" \
    git -C "$root" commit-tree "$tree" "$@"
}

save_snapshot() {
  local label=${1:-checkpoint}
  local alternate_index index_entries real_index index_tree index_commit tree commit timestamp
  local entry mode path head_entry head_mode

  case "$label" in
    ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*) die "label must use only letters, digits, dot, underscore, or dash" ;;
  esac
  timestamp=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
  saved_ref="refs/tbh/recovery/$label/$timestamp-$$"
  git check-ref-format "$saved_ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "label does not form a valid recovery ref"

  alternate_index=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tbh-recovery-index.XXXXXX")
  index_entries=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tbh-recovery-entries.XXXXXX")
  rm -f "$alternate_index"
  trap 'rm -f "$alternate_index" "$index_entries"' EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' HUP INT TERM

  real_index=$(git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-path index)
  case "$real_index" in
    /*) ;;
    *) real_index="$root/$real_index" ;;
  esac
  cp "$real_index" "$alternate_index"
  index_tree=$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$alternate_index" git -C "$root" write-tree)
  index_commit=$(
    write_recovery_commit "TBH recovery index: $label" "$index_tree" -p "$head"
  )
  rm -f "$alternate_index"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$alternate_index" git -C "$root" read-tree "$head"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$alternate_index" git -C "$root" add -A -- .
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$alternate_index" git -C "$root" ls-files --stage -z >"$index_entries"
  while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
    mode=${entry%% *}
    [ "$mode" = 160000 ] || continue
    case "$entry" in
      *$'\t'*) path=${entry#*$'\t'} ;;
      *) die "cannot inspect saved Git links" ;;
    esac
    head_entry=$(GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 git -C "$root" ls-tree "$head" -- "$path")
    head_mode=${head_entry%% *}
    [ "$head_mode" = 160000 ] ||

1|# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — WP-F: Roll out catalogue fix to live runners and purge test entries
2|
3|Task: `8c7e2d15-3f17-41a1-b905-99ca5e536c83` · Parent bug: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`
4|Source: `docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/RESPONSE.md` WP-F runbook (§4) + §6 end-to-end verification, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23/q24, `TICKETS.md` sequencing.
5|Survey input: this task's `SURVEY.md` (round 1, q1–q6, answers recorded — see §Survey mapping for actuals) + parent `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` rounds 1–2.
6|Plan type: rollout / migration (ops runbook + live-state cleanup + verification). No product code changes; docs and operator handoffs only.
7|
8|## Goal
9|
10|Bring the live fleet onto the fixed catalogue stack (WP-A + WP-B + WP-C deployed, WP-E merged) and purge test pollution from live engine state, leaving zero `test-fleet` entries and a catalogue that satisfies RESPONSE.md §6 — without the agent ever touching a running task runner itself.
11|
12|## Success Criteria
13|
14|1. Gates honoured: WP-A, WP-B, WP-C merged and deployed (backend image rebuilt to a recorded commit), WP-E merged; WP-D status recorded (preferred, not blocking); explicit human permission recorded before any live-state step.
15|2. Agent performed only pre-approved live actions: read-only checks + DELETE of test/dummy catalogue entries via the WP-C admin route. All runner reinstall / env-edit / restart steps were executed by the human operator from agent-provided instructions (never by the agent).
16|3. RESPONSE.md §6 passes end to end: §3.1 shows `discovered`/`pinned+discovered` + per-harness `ok:true`, `versions.build.sha` matches deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot: false`; §3.2 shows no `bare`/`provider` entries, no `test-fleet-model`, every entry `harnesses.length === 1`; UI checks pass; regression check passes; named `npm test` suites pass; WP-E guard proves no suite touched `~/.kainbain/engine`.
17|4. Live state contains zero `test-fleet` entries: `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` gone from `fleet-catalog.json`; revoked runner `test-fleet-muse` left revoked for audit (survey q4 asks delete-completely, but no runner-record DELETE endpoint exists — operator explicitly accepts the infeasibility or removes it out-of-band).
18|5. Execution evidence is recorded in this task's docs folder (gate record, operator handoff receipts, verification log) so WP-G can be decision-gated on it.
19|
20|## Approach
21|
22|"Make change easy, then make the change": the agent does all of the safe, reversible preparation itself (Phases 0–1: gate checks, read-only rehearsal, exact operator commands, backups, dry-run verification scripts), then hands precisely two execution bundles to the operator (Phases 2–3: reinstall/env/restart — recommended, never executed by the agent), then performs only the pre-approved purge itself (Phase 4), then verifies everything against §6 (Phase 5) and records the evidence WP-G needs (Phase 6).
23|
24|Big/risky items come first: permission + gate verification and the self-kill-safe restart sequencing are resolved before any live state is touched; the irreversible DELETE comes only after WP-E-merged is proven (no re-pollution) and backups exist.
25|
26|### Survey mapping (binding constraints)
27|
28|Parent survey (`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`):
29|
30|- q23: user pre-approved ONLY "Removing test or dummy catalogue entries". Note: "restarting local runners … would likely cause task agents to kill themselves so maybe not but maybe recommend to user to do" → agent RECOMMENDS restarts, never executes them.
31|- q24: overall structural approach approved.
32|- Carried context: q1 keep 0-runner entries indefinitely + "Remove permanently" action; q3/q4 unverified = 0 runners, selectable but marked; q7 block non-canonical ids; q8 harness-qualified ids; q15 warn-only on version mismatch (block only on real incompatibility).
33|
34|This task's `SURVEY.md` (q1–q6, answers RECORDED — actuals below, superseding the plan-time Recommended-default assumptions):
35|
36|| # | Question | Actual answer |
37||---|---|---|
38|| q1 | Agent restarting runners? | Agent suggests, operator executes (Recommended) — notes: "The main worry is that they kill themselves while executing a task if we can avoid that it's safer to execute" |
39|| q2 | Cleanup timing? | As soon as WP-A/B/C deployed + WP-E merged (Recommended) |
40|| q3 | What to delete? | Test entries PLUS old leftover entries that no runner provides (NOT the Recommended test/dummy-only) |
41|| q4 | Revoked `test-fleet-muse` runner? | Delete it completely (NOT the Recommended leave-revoked) |
42|| q5 | `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` pin list? | Remove it; discovery is source of truth (Recommended) |
43|| q6 | On any failed check? | Stop immediately and report (Recommended) |
44|
45|Binding-constraint reconciliation (agent execution scope):
46|
47|- q3 vs parent q23: parent `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23 pre-approved ONLY "removing test or dummy catalogue entries" for agent execution. The broader q3 "test-plus-leftover" scope therefore needs a FRESH explicit human grant (who/when/exact ids) before the agent may DELETE any quarantined leftover. Until that grant exists, agent DELETEs stay test/dummy-only and quarantined leftovers are left for audit (Phase 4 step 17 default stands).
48|- q4 infeasible via API: no runner-record DELETE endpoint exists (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` exposes only revoke/pause/resume + the two catalogue DELETEs; verified run17). "Delete completely" cannot be executed by the agent through any API; the revoked `test-fleet-muse` record stays for audit unless the operator removes it out-of-band. The operator must explicitly accept this infeasibility (or perform the removal themselves) — it must not be silently treated as done.
49|- q1 note ("safer to execute [if self-kill avoidable]") does NOT authorize agent-executed restarts: the restart of any runner from inside a task agent on it remains a self-kill risk, so the agent still only RECOMMENDS restarts and the operator executes them.
50|
51|If the operator overrides any q1–q6 answer at the gate, update this section and re-scope Phases 2–4 before proceeding.
52|
53|## Steps
54|
55|### Phase 0 — Gates, permission, baseline (agent, read-only). Do first.
56|
57|1. Verify blockers: confirm WP-A (`ae1ae677…`), WP-B (`77a4072e…`), WP-C (`94ee5786…`) are merged AND the backend image was rebuilt after them (record deployed commit SHA + image tag); confirm WP-E (`99ccc12f…`) merged; record WP-D (`4ec027a7…`) status (preferred, not blocking). Source of truth: task tracker states + deploy log, not memory.
58|2. Obtain and record explicit human permission for the live-state steps (Phase 4 purge + Phase 5 live reads). Minimum record: who, when, exact scope ("DELETE `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` + read-only §3/§6 checks; runner restarts by operator only"). No permission → stop here.
59|3. Confirm the q1–q6 assumptions above with the operator (one message listing the six adopted defaults + asking for corrections). Record answers.
60|4. Baseline snapshot (read-only): run RESPONSE.md §3.1–§3.4 verbatim; save outputs to `docs/tasks/8c7e2d15-3f17-41a1-b905-99ca5e536c83/baseline-<date>.md`. Also copy (never move) live state to timestamped backups: `~/.kainbain/engine/runners.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/fleet-catalog.json` → operator-owned backup dir; record paths + shasum. Backups are the rollback path for Phase 4.
61|5. Inventory runners: list every `local-*` runner, its service definition / launch script, its env file (`~/.kainbain/runner-local-*.env`), and `server2-alpha`'s install location + pi-leg state. Record which installs run from the engine checkout (the N1 failure: RESPONSE.md §2.2 N1, `daemon.js` replaced 4 s after boot) vs a dedicated dir.
62|
63|Gate: all of Phase 0 recorded. Any gate fail (blocker unmerged, no permission, WP-E not merged) → stop, report, do not proceed.

66|
67|6. Each bundle: purpose, exact commands, expected output, rollback (prior install path / env backup).
69|8. Design the self-kill-safe restart sequence and put it in the handoff doc: operator picks a quiescent window (no active task agents on the runner being restarted), restarts ONE runner at a time, confirms re-registration + healthy `discoveryStatus` before the next. Never restart all runners at once; never restart the runner executing this task's agent from inside that agent (this is why the agent never runs these commands itself — q23 note).
70|9. Dry-run the Phase 4 purge + Phase 5 checks against fixtures (not live): exercise `DELETE /runners/models/catalogue/:id` semantics (204/404) and the §6 assertions against a temp copy of the catalogue / `createFleetModelSnapshotStore({filePath: null})` output. Prepare the literal §6 checklist commands (Phase 5) so execution is mechanical.

Write the operator handoff document to this task's docs folder (`operator-handoff-<date>.md`): the Phase 2–3 bundles, the restart sequence, what to report back (per-runner: new `versions.build.sha`, `discoveryStatus`, `modelSource`), and the explicit statement that the agent will not execute these steps.
72|
73|Gate: handoff doc reviewed. Operator acknowledges receipt before Phase 2.

77|11. 173|`pinned+discovered`), `discoveryStatus` (expect one key per configured
174|harness, `ok:true` or a NAMED error code — never `{}`, never absent),
175|`versions.build.sha` (expect THE STAMPED sha of the bundle that runner
176|installed — `fbcf8442…`-series for the .206 local runners IF rebuilt
177|from main@`fbcf8442`, `de62122c…` for server2-alpha from the staged
178|tarball above; the sha NEVER comes from the tarball filename; ALSO
179|report the deploy-log true backend commit for the §6.1 comparison),
180|`codeChangedSinceBoot` (expect false), and `paused` (expect false for
181|every serving runner — a paused runner keeps `status: active` and
182|still queues `requestModelRediscovery` (202), but its discovery never
183|reaches the catalogue or dispatch, so leaving one paused is a fleet
184|decision that must be recorded as intent, not left as an accident).
185|
186|STOP rules (q6): any runner reporting `LEG_MODULE_MISSING`, `NOT_YET_RUN`
187|(after a completed round), a stale `build.sha`, or `codeChangedSinceBoot:
188|true` → stop, diagnose with the agent, do NOT proceed to purge. Purge +
189|§6 need a fresh agent run holding explicit recorded permission.
190|`codeChangedSinceBoot:true` triage (the daemon fingerprints its tree at
191|boot — file count, total bytes, newest mtime, skipping `.git` and
192|`node_modules` — and re-scans every heartbeat, so `true` means a file
193|under the install was provably added, removed, or rewritten after
194|boot): on the runner host run `find <install-dir> -newermt
195|'<boot-time>' -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -not -path '*/.git/*'`
196|(boot time ≈ `versions.bootedAtMs`, or the process start from
197|`systemctl --user status <unit>`). A benign inspection artifact or
198|runtime write → record it and re-baseline with a quiescent restart; an
199|unexpected code change → treat as N1-class drift: reinstall from the
200|bundle, do NOT just restart over it.
201|
202|## Phase 4 transfer note (agent executes, operator permits — read before granting)
203|
204|The purge agent runs (URL-encoded id):
205|`DELETE /runners/models/catalogue/<id>` → 204 gone, 404
206|`UNKNOWN_MODEL` already absent (both are non-errors for the purge
207|target); `DELETE /runners/models/catalogue/quarantine/<id>` likewise
208|for quarantined rows. A re-advertised id legitimately reappears on the
209|next snapshot update — absence is confirmed by a fresh GET, never by
210|the DELETE status alone. Auth: both routes need the admin role, and
211|API keys are explicitly refused (`allowApiKeys: false` — keys get 403
212|`forbidden`); while access control is OFF (current live state) the
213|routes are open. If access control is ever ON, 401/403 means "auth",
214|NOT "absent" — the purge run must use a human admin session, and a
215|403 must never be misread as purge-complete. There is deliberately NO
216|runner-record DELETE endpoint (only revoke/pause/resume), so a
217|"delete the revoked runner completely" grant is infeasible via API —
218|revoked records stay for audit.
219|
220|## Addendum 2026-11-14 (agent safe action) — systemd user-level pin trap
221|
222|`~/.kainbain/runner-local-{alpha,bravo}.env` is NOT the only source of
223|`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`. `local-alpha` was inheriting a 17-model pin
224|from the systemd *user* environment (`systemctl --user show-environment`),
225|so the env-file removal alone never took effect and the upgraded daemon
226|kept reporting `modelSource: pinned` with `discoveryStatus: {}`. Bravo did
227|not inherit it. Before restarting any runner, the operator MUST:
228|
229|```bash
230|systemctl --user unset-environment KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS
231|# also check persistence:
232|grep -R KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS ~/.config/environment.d 2>/dev/null || true
233|```
234|
235|Only after the user environment is clean will a post-WP-B restart flip
236|`modelSource` to `discovered`/`pinned+discovered`.
237|
238|## Addendum 2026-11-17 (cleanup-stage hardening — operator-visible behavior changes)
239|
240|The cleanup stage hardened the exact tools this handoff runs. No step above
241|changes meaning; the tools now fail safe where WP-F hit confusion:
242|
243|- `scripts/package-runner.sh` refuses a sha-looking REF that matches
244|  neither HEAD nor its short form (the `fbcf8442`-filename-vs-`de62122c`-
245|  stamp trap). Either check out the REF first, pass the HEAD short sha,
246|  or re-run with `--allow-ref-mismatch` when you mean it. Every build
247|  now prints a transfer receipt (`sha256:` + `stamped build.sha:`) —
248|  re-hash before install, and compare receipts against the STAMPED sha,
249|  never the filename.
250|- `lay_down_runner_install_root` (Bundle A wrapper installs) now asserts
251|  the laid-down tree (`runner/main.js`, both `version.json` copies, the
252|  wrapper shim) before `current` may point at it, and warns when the
253|  tree ships no pi discovery dependency (pi-serving runners will report
254|  `LEG_MODULE_MISSING` until reinstalled from a real bundle;
255|  muse/antigravity/vibe-only hosts are unaffected).
256|- `codeChangedSinceBoot` no longer flips on non-code artifacts left by
257|  inspection (`*.bak*`, `*~`, `*.log`, `*.tmp`, OS junk) — the false
258|  positive that forced the run24 local-alpha re-baseline. It now scans
259|  the whole bundle root (`version.json` + `runner/` + `api/` + `shared/`)
260|  for installed bundles instead of `runner/` alone, so harness-code
261|  drift under `api/` is visible — matching the `find <install-dir>`
262|  triage above. Scan the unpacked bundle root
263|  (`.../releases/<ver>/unpacked`, or the direct install dir) with that
264|  `find`, not the wrapper root, for the tightest match to the daemon.

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash
   bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard
   ```

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash
bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore <recovery-ref>
```

Restore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real
index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could
not save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.

## Always fine

Read-only inspection such as `status`, `log`, `show`, `diff`, `blame`,
`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.
Staging named files to inspect `diff --cached`, and a temporary stash around a
tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

## The rest

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.
- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing
  source-control trees.
- Do not create or edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` to hide the user's
  files, and do not stash the user's files (including `stash push -u`) to make
  `git status` look clean. "Leave the working tree clean", "tidy up", and
  similar phrasing do not authorize committing, pushing, ignoring, excluding,
  stashing, or deleting the user's files; clean up only scratch you created
  and say the user's files remain.
- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.
- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

## Locks and corrupt state

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

Never commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot
explain.

## If you already made an unwanted write

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash
   bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard
   ```

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash
bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore <recovery-ref>
```

Restore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real
index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could
not save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.

## Always fine

Read-only inspection such as `status`, `log`, `show`, `diff`, `blame`,
`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.
Staging named files to inspect `diff --cached`, and a temporary stash around a
tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

## The rest

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.
- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing
  source-control trees.
- Do not create or edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` to hide the user's
  files, and do not stash the user's files (including `stash push -u`) to make
  `git status` look clean. "Leave the working tree clean", "tidy up", and
  similar phrasing do not authorize committing, pushing, ignoring, excluding,
  stashing, or deleting the user's files; clean up only scratch you created
  and say the user's files remain.
- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.
- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

## Locks and corrupt state

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

Never commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot
explain.

## If you already made an unwanted write

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.

1|# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — WP-F: Roll out catalogue fix to live runners and purge test entries
2|
3|Task: `8c7e2d15-3f17-41a1-b905-99ca5e536c83` · Parent bug: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`
4|Source: `docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/RESPONSE.md` WP-F runbook (§4) + §6 end-to-end verification, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23/q24, `TICKETS.md` sequencing.
5|Survey input: this task's `SURVEY.md` (round 1, q1–q6, answers recorded — see §Survey mapping for actuals) + parent `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` rounds 1–2.
6|Plan type: rollout / migration (ops runbook + live-state cleanup + verification). No product code changes; docs and operator handoffs only.
7|
8|## Goal
9|
10|Bring the live fleet onto the fixed catalogue stack (WP-A + WP-B + WP-C deployed, WP-E merged) and purge test pollution from live engine state, leaving zero `test-fleet` entries and a catalogue that satisfies RESPONSE.md §6 — without the agent ever touching a running task runner itself.
11|
12|## Success Criteria
13|
14|1. Gates honoured: WP-A, WP-B, WP-C merged and deployed (backend image rebuilt to a recorded commit), WP-E merged; WP-D status recorded (preferred, not blocking); explicit human permission recorded before any live-state step.
15|2. Agent performed only pre-approved live actions: read-only checks + DELETE of test/dummy catalogue entries via the WP-C admin route. All runner reinstall / env-edit / restart steps were executed by the human operator from agent-provided instructions (never by the agent).
16|3. RESPONSE.md §6 passes end to end: §3.1 shows `discovered`/`pinned+discovered` + per-harness `ok:true`, `versions.build.sha` matches deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot: false`; §3.2 shows no `bare`/`provider` entries, no `test-fleet-model`, every entry `harnesses.length === 1`; UI checks pass; regression check passes; named `npm test` suites pass; WP-E guard proves no suite touched `~/.kainbain/engine`.
17|4. Live state contains zero `test-fleet` entries: `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` gone from `fleet-catalog.json`; revoked runner `test-fleet-muse` left revoked for audit (survey q4 asks delete-completely, but no runner-record DELETE endpoint exists — operator explicitly accepts the infeasibility or removes it out-of-band).
18|5. Execution evidence is recorded in this task's docs folder (gate record, operator handoff receipts, verification log) so WP-G can be decision-gated on it.
19|
20|## Approach
21|
22|"Make change easy, then make the change": the agent does all of the safe, reversible preparation itself (Phases 0–1: gate checks, read-only rehearsal, exact operator commands, backups, dry-run verification scripts), then hands precisely two execution bundles to the operator (Phases 2–3: reinstall/env/restart — recommended, never executed by the agent), then performs only the pre-approved purge itself (Phase 4), then verifies everything against §6 (Phase 5) and records the evidence WP-G needs (Phase 6).
23|
24|Big/risky items come first: permission + gate verification and the self-kill-safe restart sequencing are resolved before any live state is touched; the irreversible DELETE comes only after WP-E-merged is proven (no re-pollution) and backups exist.
25|
26|### Survey mapping (binding constraints)
27|
28|Parent survey (`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`):
29|
30|- q23: user pre-approved ONLY "Removing test or dummy catalogue entries". Note: "restarting local runners … would likely cause task agents to kill themselves so maybe not but maybe recommend to user to do" → agent RECOMMENDS restarts, never executes them.
31|- q24: overall structural approach approved.
32|- Carried context: q1 keep 0-runner entries indefinitely + "Remove permanently" action; q3/q4 unverified = 0 runners, selectable but marked; q7 block non-canonical ids; q8 harness-qualified ids; q15 warn-only on version mismatch (block only on real incompatibility).
33|
34|This task's `SURVEY.md` (q1–q6, answers RECORDED — actuals below, superseding the plan-time Recommended-default assumptions):
35|
36|| # | Question | Actual answer |
37||---|---|---|
38|| q1 | Agent restarting runners? | Agent suggests, operator executes (Recommended) — notes: "The main worry is that they kill themselves while executing a task if we can avoid that it's safer to execute" |
39|| q2 | Cleanup timing? | As soon as WP-A/B/C deployed + WP-E merged (Recommended) |
40|| q3 | What to delete? | Test entries PLUS old leftover entries that no runner provides (NOT the Recommended test/dummy-only) |
41|| q4 | Revoked `test-fleet-muse` runner? | Delete it completely (NOT the Recommended leave-revoked) |
42|| q5 | `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` pin list? | Remove it; discovery is source of truth (Recommended) |
43|| q6 | On any failed check? | Stop immediately and report (Recommended) |
44|
45|Binding-constraint reconciliation (agent execution scope):
46|
47|- q3 vs parent q23: parent `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23 pre-approved ONLY "removing test or dummy catalogue entries" for agent execution. The broader q3 "test-plus-leftover" scope therefore needs a FRESH explicit human grant (who/when/exact ids) before the agent may DELETE any quarantined leftover. Until that grant exists, agent DELETEs stay test/dummy-only and quarantined leftovers are left for audit (Phase 4 step 17 default stands).
48|- q4 infeasible via API: no runner-record DELETE endpoint exists (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` exposes only revoke/pause/resume + the two catalogue DELETEs; verified run17). "Delete completely" cannot be executed by the agent through any API; the revoked `test-fleet-muse` record stays for audit unless the operator removes it out-of-band. The operator must explicitly accept this infeasibility (or perform the removal themselves) — it must not be silently treated as done.
49|- q1 note ("safer to execute [if self-kill avoidable]") does NOT authorize agent-executed restarts: the restart of any runner from inside a task agent on it remains a self-kill risk, so the agent still only RECOMMENDS restarts and the operator executes them.
50|
51|If the operator overrides any q1–q6 answer at the gate, update this section and re-scope Phases 2–4 before proceeding.
52|
53|## Steps
54|
55|### Phase 0 — Gates, permission, baseline (agent, read-only). Do first.
56|
57|1. Verify blockers: confirm WP-A (`ae1ae677…`), WP-B (`77a4072e…`), WP-C (`94ee5786…`) are merged AND the backend image was rebuilt after them (record deployed commit SHA + image tag); confirm WP-E (`99ccc12f…`) merged; record WP-D (`4ec027a7…`) status (preferred, not blocking). Source of truth: task tracker states + deploy log, not memory.
58|2. Obtain and record explicit human permission for the live-state steps (Phase 4 purge + Phase 5 live reads). Minimum record: who, when, exact scope ("DELETE `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` + read-only §3/§6 checks; runner restarts by operator only"). No permission → stop here.
59|3. Confirm the q1–q6 assumptions above with the operator (one message listing the six adopted defaults + asking for corrections). Record answers.
60|4. Baseline snapshot (read-only): run RESPONSE.md §3.1–§3.4 verbatim; save outputs to `docs/tasks/8c7e2d15-3f17-41a1-b905-99ca5e536c83/baseline-<date>.md`. Also copy (never move) live state to timestamped backups: `~/.kainbain/engine/runners.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/fleet-catalog.json` → operator-owned backup dir; record paths + shasum. Backups are the rollback path for Phase 4.
61|5. Inventory runners: list every `local-*` runner, its service definition / launch script, its env file (`~/.kainbain/runner-local-*.env`), and `server2-alpha`'s install location + pi-leg state. Record which installs run from the engine checkout (the N1 failure: RESPONSE.md §2.2 N1, `daemon.js` replaced 4 s after boot) vs a dedicated dir.
62|
63|Gate: all of Phase 0 recorded. Any gate fail (blocker unmerged, no permission, WP-E not merged) → stop, report, do not proceed.
64|
65|### Phase 1 — Make the change easy (agent, no live state). Do second.
66|
67|6. Rehearse §3 read-only checks end to end and confirm they reproduce the "before" picture (§3.1 `pinned` + `{}`, §3.2 bare/provider + `test-fleet-model`, §3.3 checkout cwd + missing `harnessModelDiscovery.js`, §3.4 isolation gap closed post-WP-E). Fix any stale paths (RESPONSE.md used `/home/[REDACTED]/...`; this host's engine state is under `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/engine` — verify and use the real path).

Draft the exact operator command bundles (Phase 2–3 handoff doc): reinstall-from-bundle commands per runner (`runner/updates` mechanism / `scripts/package-runner.mjs` + `scripts/install-local-runner.sh` paths verified against the deployed tree), target dirs (`~/.kainbain/runner-install/<runnerId>/`), service-definition edits for `local-alpha`/`local-bravo`/any `local-*`, env-file edits (REMOVE `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` per q5 default; fallback: trim to harness-qualified ids only), `server2-alpha` pi-leg reinstall + `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY` provider-config check. Each bundle: purpose, exact commands, expected output, rollback (prior install path / env backup).
69|8. Design the self-kill-safe restart sequence and put it in the handoff doc: operator picks a quiescent window (no active task agents on the runner being restarted), restarts ONE runner at a time, confirms re-registration + healthy `discoveryStatus` before the next. Never restart all runners at once; never restart the runner executing this task's agent from inside that agent (this is why the agent never runs these commands itself — q23 note).
70|9. Dry-run the Phase 4 purge + Phase 5 checks against fixtures (not live): exercise `DELETE /runners/models/catalogue/:id` semantics (204/404) and the §6 assertions against a temp copy of the catalogue / `createFleetModelSnapshotStore({filePath: null})` output. Prepare the literal §6 checklist commands (Phase 5) so execution is mechanical.
71|10. Write the operator handoff document to this task's docs folder (`operator-handoff-<date>.md`): the Phase 2–3 bundles, the restart sequence, what to report back (per-runner: new `versions.build.sha`, `discoveryStatus`, `modelSource`), and the explicit statement that the agent will not execute these steps.
72|
73|Gate: handoff doc reviewed. Operator acknowledges receipt before Phase 2.

75|### Phase 2 — Runner reinstall + config (OPERATOR executes, agent only wrote the instructions)
76|
77|11. Operator installs each `local-*` runner from the post-WP-B RUNNER BUNDLE into its dedicated directory (never from the engine checkout `…/runner-work/…/runner`), updates service definitions/launch scripts, and edits each `~/.kainbain/runner-local-*.env` (remove `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` recommended).
78|12. Operator reinstalls `server2-alpha` from the post-WP-B bundle so the pi leg dependency (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`) resolves, and checks the Muse MSP provider config (`MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY`).
79|13. Operator reports back per-runner: install path, bundle version, env diff. Agent records the receipt; agent runs NO commands on the runners.
80|
81|### Phase 3 — Restart + rediscovery (OPERATOR executes, agent only wrote the instructions)
82|
83|14. Operator restarts runners ONE at a time in a quiescent window per the Phase 1 sequence, then triggers `requestModelRediscovery` from Settings.
84|15. Operator reports back per-runner: `modelSource`, `discoveryStatus` (expect a key per configured harness, `ok:true` or a named error code, never `{}`), `versions.build.sha` vs deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot`. Agent records the receipt. If any runner reports `LEG_MODULE_MISSING` / `NOT_YET_RUN` / stale code → stop, diagnose with operator, do not proceed to purge (per q6 stop-immediately).
85|
86|### Phase 4 — Purge test pollution (agent, pre-approved scope only)
87|
88|Preconditions (re-check immediately before): Phase 0 permission on file, WP-E merged (no re-pollution), backups from step 4 exist, Phase 3 receipts show healthy discovery.
89|
90|16. DELETE `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` via the WP-C admin route (`DELETE /runners/models/catalogue/:id`, URL-encoded id; expect 204). Confirm absence in a fresh `GET /runners/models/catalogue` (and in `fleet-catalog.json`).
91|17. Quarantine: quarantined bare/provider ids — remove via `DELETE …/quarantine/:id` ONLY on a fresh explicit human grant naming the q3 test-plus-leftover scope (who/when/exact ids); otherwise leave for audit and record the decision. (Default: leave; agent execution stays test/dummy-only per parent q23 until that grant exists.)
92|18. Revoked runner `test-fleet-muse`: leave revoked for audit. Survey q4 asks "delete completely" but NO runner-record DELETE endpoint exists, so the agent cannot execute this via any API; record the operator's explicit acceptance of that infeasibility (or their out-of-band removal) — never silently treat it as done.
93|19. Re-run §3.2 immediately: expect zero `bare`/`provider` entries in `models`, zero `test-fleet-model`, every entry `harnesses.length === 1`. Any miss → stop per q6.
94|
95|### Phase 5 — Section-6 verification (agent: live reads + suites; operator: UI pass)
96|
97|20. §6.1 — runner health: §3.1 shows `discovered`/`pinned+discovered`, per-harness `ok:true` (or named error, never `{}`), `versions.build.sha` == deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot: false`.
98|21. §6.2 — catalogue hygiene: §3.2 clean as in step 19.
99|22. §6.3 — UI pass (operator or headless check, no long-lived servers — see Validation Plan): Project Settings → Muse Code harness badge reads "N runners"; model list contains `muse-ember` (or current `muse serve` output) with "N runners"; no `gemma4`/`deepseek`/`test-fleet-model`; dropped models show grey "0 runners" with "Remove permanently" in Settings.
100|23. §6.4 — regression: remove a model from a fake leg's output → entry stays at "0 runners" (not deleted); admin DELETE → gone; re-advertise → back.
101|24. §6.5 — suites: `npm test` for `runner/`, `api/flow/dispatch/`, `api/routes/projects.*`, `fleetModelOptions`, `ModelSelector.test.jsx`; WP-E guard proves no suite touched `~/.kainbain/engine`. See Validation Plan for exact invocations.
102|25. Per q6: ANY check fails → stop immediately, report which check + evidence, do not continue to WP-G. Record pass/fail per check in `verification-<date>.md`.
103|
104|### Phase 6 — Documentation + WP-G gate (agent)
105|
106|26. Write `verification-<date>.md` (per-check evidence: commands + outputs) and update this plan's Survey-mapping + gate records with actuals.
107|27. Write the WP-G readiness note: does every live runner report healthy discovery? (WP-G may proceed to its human dispatch decision only on yes.) WP-G ticket: `6ba7e727-8b7a-4c46-ad4a-960bcd099bcb`.
108|28. Non-goals respected: no dispatch changes (WP-G owns `buildFleetModelCatalog`/`runnerMatches`/`confirmRunnerModel` claimability); no frontend changes (WP-D owns pickers); no backend contract changes (WP-C owns ingest/snapshot); no test-isolation changes (WP-E owns them).

110|## Validation Plan
111|
112|- Pre-change rehearsal: §3.1–§3.4 read-only commands (RESPONSE.md §3, with host-corrected state paths) reproduce the documented "before" state; outputs saved as baseline. No live mutation.
113|- Purge correctness: `GET /runners/models/catalogue` before/after diff shows exactly one removal (`muse::meta::test-fleet-model`); §3.2 script returns zero rows; `grep -r test-fleet` over `~/.kainbain/engine/*.json` returns nothing except the intentionally retained revoked runner record (if q4 default kept).
114|- Runner health (§6.1): per-runner `modelSource`, `discoveryStatus`, `versions.build` (incl. `codeChangedSinceBoot`) asserted from `runners.json` + Settings runner card (WP-A warning renders on mismatch).
115|- UI (§6.3): prefer the headless screenshot tool (`npm run capture:screenshot`) or existing `ModelSelector`/`fleetModelOptions` fixtures over any live server; if a live UI look is needed, the operator performs it (agent does not spawn long-lived background servers per stage guidance).
116|- Regression (§6.4): fake-leg removal → "0 runners" persists; admin DELETE → 204 + absent; re-advertise → present again. Run against the-live-but-backed-up catalogue only after Phase 4; otherwise against fixture store first.
117|- Suites (§6.5): run the project's own gates — `npm run test:unit` (api + frontend) at minimum, scoped to at least: `runner/`, `api/flow/dispatch/`, `api/routes/projects.*`, `frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions`, `frontend/src/components/common/ModelSelector.test.jsx`; plus the WP-E guard test. Highest-risk validation: §6.1 per-harness `ok:true` on every live runner (it gates both purge confidence and WP-G).
118|- Rollback: restore the two state files from Phase 0 backups; reinstall prior runner bundle / restore env backups (operator); re-trigger `requestModelRediscovery`; re-run §3.1/§3.2 to confirm pre-change state. Rollback is tested as a dry run against copies in Phase 1, never against live state speculatively.

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included. When the user opened by saying they want to understand
or design first, a later message that only adds a requirement or constraint is more
design input, not the signal to start: answer how it shapes the design and the
choices still open, and change files once the user says to build it.

When the user asks whether built behavior is correct, the report is a bug fix
only for what you prove wrong. Check each observation against the source the
project follows: its specification, its documentation, or the real-world rules
it simulates. Fix what that source shows is wrong. When it shows an observation
is correct, keep that behavior, tell the user why it is correct, and offer the
change instead of making it. Do not remove correct behavior to make a reported
symptom go away, even to keep the project simpler.

Loading it does not settle what the new behavior should be either. A test fixes
one answer, so when the request leaves a choice about the delivered behavior to
the user (for example what an output meant for another person or system
includes) and the repository's existing precedents disagree on it, ask that one
grouped question before writing the test or the code; do not pick a reading and
record it in a test.

## Find the code the report is about

A focused test pins the place where the user hit the problem. When a report
could fit more than one place in the code (two clients or two copies of one
feature) and does not say where it was seen, find out which one before writing
the test: read the user's own open changes and tasks and the candidate files'
history. A shallow local clone lacks that history, so read it through the code
host's CLI when the environment has one. Picking the file whose wording fits
the report best, or testing and fixing every candidate to be safe, skips this
step; once you know where the user saw it, fix there and every other place the
same root cause reaches.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: a
focused failing test for each reported defect, the fix, those tests passing,
and, when a broad run is required, one broad run after the final edit.
Smallest limits the machinery, not the cases: add no new framework, suite, or
repeated broad run, but let the maintained test cover the inputs the fix
claims to handle beyond the reported one, such as another position or order,
extreme or boundary values, and each input rule the request restates. When the behavior is output that arrives over time (a stream, a paced or follow mode, progress lines), the test reads the first record through the user-facing command while that command is still running, with a bounded read: a test that captures the output after the command exits passes even when every line arrived together when the command exited. A rule the request tells you to keep, such as input validation, counts as restated: for each function the fix rewrites, give every argument that rule checks its own rejected-input case, since an existing case for one function or argument does not cover the others. A report
that something already built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes
with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn that this workflow still covers (see Scale to the task),
update the maintained test even when the old suite remains green and the user
does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior, not merely an
unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.
When the request names failing tests, run each one after the final edit in
the configuration it was reported failing in (build mode, platform, flags); the
same test under another configuration is a different check, not a repeat, and
its pass does not prove the named one.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

A runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. When the
repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.

1|# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — WP-F: Roll out catalogue fix to live runners and purge test entries
2|
3|Task: `8c7e2d15-3f17-41a1-b905-99ca5e536c83` · Parent bug: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`
4|Source: `docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/RESPONSE.md` WP-F runbook (§4) + §6 end-to-end verification, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23/q24, `TICKETS.md` sequencing.
5|Survey input: this task's `SURVEY.md` (round 1, q1–q6, answers recorded — see §Survey mapping for actuals) + parent `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` rounds 1–2.
6|Plan type: rollout / migration (ops runbook + live-state cleanup + verification). No product code changes; docs and operator handoffs only.
7|
8|## Goal
9|
10|Bring the live fleet onto the fixed catalogue stack (WP-A + WP-B + WP-C deployed, WP-E merged) and purge test pollution from live engine state, leaving zero `test-fleet` entries and a catalogue that satisfies RESPONSE.md §6 — without the agent ever touching a running task runner itself.
11|
12|## Success Criteria
13|
14|1. Gates honoured: WP-A, WP-B, WP-C merged and deployed (backend image rebuilt to a recorded commit), WP-E merged; WP-D status recorded (preferred, not blocking); explicit human permission recorded before any live-state step.
15|2. Agent performed only pre-approved live actions: read-only checks + DELETE of test/dummy catalogue entries via the WP-C admin route. All runner reinstall / env-edit / restart steps were executed by the human operator from agent-provided instructions (never by the agent).
16|3. RESPONSE.md §6 passes end to end: §3.1 shows `discovered`/`pinned+discovered` + per-harness `ok:true`, `versions.build.sha` matches deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot: false`; §3.2 shows no `bare`/`provider` entries, no `test-fleet-model`, every entry `harnesses.length === 1`; UI checks pass; regression check passes; named `npm test` suites pass; WP-E guard proves no suite touched `~/.kainbain/engine`.
17|4. Live state contains zero `test-fleet` entries: `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` gone from `fleet-catalog.json`; revoked runner `test-fleet-muse` left revoked for audit (survey q4 asks delete-completely, but no runner-record DELETE endpoint exists — operator explicitly accepts the infeasibility or removes it out-of-band).
18|5. Execution evidence is recorded in this task's docs folder (gate record, operator handoff receipts, verification log) so WP-G can be decision-gated on it.
19|
20|## Approach
21|
22|"Make change easy, then make the change": the agent does all of the safe, reversible preparation itself (Phases 0–1: gate checks, read-only rehearsal, exact operator commands, backups, dry-run verification scripts), then hands precisely two execution bundles to the operator (Phases 2–3: reinstall/env/restart — recommended, never executed by the agent), then performs only the pre-approved purge itself (Phase 4), then verifies everything against §6 (Phase 5) and records the evidence WP-G needs (Phase 6).
23|
24|Big/risky items come first: permission + gate verification and the self-kill-safe restart sequencing are resolved before any live state is touched; the irreversible DELETE comes only after WP-E-merged is proven (no re-pollution) and backups exist.
25|
26|### Survey mapping (binding constraints)
27|
28|Parent survey (`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`):
29|
30|- q23: user pre-approved ONLY "Removing test or dummy catalogue entries". Note: "restarting local runners … would likely cause task agents to kill themselves so maybe not but maybe recommend to user to do" → agent RECOMMENDS restarts, never executes them.
31|- q24: overall structural approach approved.
32|- Carried context: q1 keep 0-runner entries indefinitely + "Remove permanently" action; q3/q4 unverified = 0 runners, selectable but marked; q7 block non-canonical ids; q8 harness-qualified ids; q15 warn-only on version mismatch (block only on real incompatibility).
33|
34|This task's `SURVEY.md` (q1–q6, answers RECORDED — actuals below, superseding the plan-time Recommended-default assumptions):
35|
36|| # | Question | Actual answer |
37||---|---|---|
38|| q1 | Agent restarting runners? | Agent suggests, operator executes (Recommended) — notes: "The main worry is that they kill themselves while executing a task if we can avoid that it's safer to execute" |
39|| q2 | Cleanup timing? | As soon as WP-A/B/C deployed + WP-E merged (Recommended) |
40|| q3 | What to delete? | Test entries PLUS old leftover entries that no runner provides (NOT the Recommended test/dummy-only) |
41|| q4 | Revoked `test-fleet-muse` runner? | Delete it completely (NOT the Recommended leave-revoked) |
42|| q5 | `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` pin list? | Remove it; discovery is source of truth (Recommended) |
43|| q6 | On any failed check? | Stop immediately and report (Recommended) |
44|
45|Binding-constraint reconciliation (agent execution scope):
46|
47|- q3 vs parent q23: parent `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q23 pre-approved ONLY "removing test or dummy catalogue entries" for agent execution. The broader q3 "test-plus-leftover" scope therefore needs a FRESH explicit human grant (who/when/exact ids) before the agent may DELETE any quarantined leftover. Until that grant exists, agent DELETEs stay test/dummy-only and quarantined leftovers are left for audit (Phase 4 step 17 default stands).
48|- q4 infeasible via API: no runner-record DELETE endpoint exists (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` exposes only revoke/pause/resume + the two catalogue DELETEs; verified run17). "Delete completely" cannot be executed by the agent through any API; the revoked `test-fleet-muse` record stays for audit unless the operator removes it out-of-band. The operator must explicitly accept this infeasibility (or perform the removal themselves) — it must not be silently treated as done.
49|- q1 note ("safer to execute [if self-kill avoidable]") does NOT authorize agent-executed restarts: the restart of any runner from inside a task agent on it remains a self-kill risk, so the agent still only RECOMMENDS restarts and the operator executes them.
50|
51|If the operator overrides any q1–q6 answer at the gate, update this section and re-scope Phases 2–4 before proceeding.
52|
53|## Steps
54|
55|### Phase 0 — Gates, permission, baseline (agent, read-only). Do first.
56|
57|1. Verify blockers: confirm WP-A (`ae1ae677…`), WP-B (`77a4072e…`), WP-C (`94ee5786…`) are merged AND the backend image was rebuilt after them (record deployed commit SHA + image tag); confirm WP-E (`99ccc12f…`) merged; record WP-D (`4ec027a7…`) status (preferred, not blocking). Source of truth: task tracker states + deploy log, not memory.
58|2. Obtain and record explicit human permission for the live-state steps (Phase 4 purge + Phase 5 live reads). Minimum record: who, when, exact scope ("DELETE `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` + read-only §3/§6 checks; runner restarts by operator only"). No permission → stop here.
59|3. Confirm the q1–q6 assumptions above with the operator (one message listing the six adopted defaults + asking for corrections). Record answers.
60|4. Baseline snapshot (read-only): run RESPONSE.md §3.1–§3.4 verbatim; save outputs to `docs/tasks/8c7e2d15-3f17-41a1-b905-99ca5e536c83/baseline-<date>.md`. Also copy (never move) live state to timestamped backups: `~/.kainbain/engine/runners.json`, `~/.kainbain/engine/fleet-catalog.json` → operator-owned backup dir; record paths + shasum. Backups are the rollback path for Phase 4.
61|5. Inventory runners: list every `local-*` runner, its service definition / launch script, its env file (`~/.kainbain/runner-local-*.env`), and `server2-alpha`'s install location + pi-leg state. Record which installs run from the engine checkout (the N1 failure: RESPONSE.md §2.2 N1, `daemon.js` replaced 4 s after boot) vs a dedicated dir.
62|

66|
67|6. Rehearse §3 read-only checks end to end and confirm they reproduce the "before" picture (§3.1 `pinned` + `{}`, §3.2 bare/provider + `test-fleet-model`, §3.3 checkout cwd + missing `harnessModelDiscovery.js`, §3.4 isolation gap closed post-WP-E). Fix any stale paths (RESPONSE.md used `/home/[REDACTED]/...`; this host's engine state is under `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/engine` — verify and use the real path).
68|7. Draft the exact operator command bundles (Phase 2–3 handoff doc): reinstall-from-bundle commands per runner (`runner/updates` mechanism / `scripts/package-runner.mjs` + `scripts/install-local-runner.sh` paths verified against the deployed tree), target dirs (`~/.kainbain/runner-install/<runnerId>/`), service-definition edits for `local-alpha`/`local-bravo`/any `local-*`, env-file edits (REMOVE `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` per q5 default; fallback: trim to harness-qualified ids only), `server2-alpha` pi-leg reinstall + `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY` provider-config check. Each bundle: purpose, exact commands, expected output, rollback (prior install path / env backup).
69|8. Design the self-kill-safe restart sequence and put it in the handoff doc: operator picks a quiescent window (no active task agents on the runner being restarted), restarts ONE runner at a time, confirms re-registration + healthy `discoveryStatus` before the next. Never restart all runners at once; never restart the runner executing this task's agent from inside that agent (this is why the agent never runs these commands itself — q23 note).

Dry-run the Phase 4 purge + Phase 5 checks against fixtures (not live): exercise `DELETE /runners/models/catalogue/:id` semantics (204/404) and the §6 assertions against a temp copy of the catalogue / `createFleetModelSnapshotStore({filePath: null})` output. Write the operator handoff document to this task's docs folder (`operator-handoff-<date>.md`): the Phase 2–3 bundles, the restart sequence, what to report back (per-runner: new `versions.build.sha`, `discoveryStatus`, `modelSource`), and the explicit statement that the agent will not execute these steps.

83|14. Operator restarts runners ONE at a time in a quiescent window per the Phase 1 sequence, then triggers `requestModelRediscovery` from Settings.

Operator reports back per-runner: `modelSource`, `discoveryStatus` (expect a key per configured harness, `ok:true` or a named error code, never `{}`), `versions.build.sha` vs deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot`. Agent records the receipt. If any runner reports `LEG_MODULE_MISSING` / `NOT_YET_RUN` / stale code → stop, diagnose with operator, do not proceed to purge (per q6 stop-immediately).

87|
88|Preconditions (re-check immediately before): Phase 0 permission on file, WP-E merged (no re-pollution), backups from step 4 exist, Phase 3 receipts show healthy discovery.

Quarantine: quarantined bare/provider ids — remove via `DELETE …/quarantine/:id` ONLY on a fresh explicit human grant naming the q3 test-plus-leftover scope (who/when/exact ids); otherwise leave for audit and record the decision. (Default: leave; agent execution stays test/dummy-only per parent q23 until that grant exists.)
92|18. Revoked runner `test-fleet-muse`: leave revoked for audit. Survey q4 asks "delete completely" but NO runner-record DELETE endpoint exists, so the agent cannot execute this via any API; record the operator's explicit acceptance of that infeasibility (or their out-of-band removal) — never silently treat it as done.
93|19. Re-run §3.2 immediately: expect zero `bare`/`provider` entries in `models`, zero `test-fleet-model`, every entry `harnesses.length === 1`. Any miss → stop per q6.
94|
95|### Phase 5 — Section-6 verification (agent: live reads + suites; operator: UI pass)
96|
97|20. §6.1 — runner health: §3.1 shows `discovered`/`pinned+discovered`, per-harness `ok:true` (or named error, never `{}`), `versions.build.sha` == deployed commit, `codeChangedSinceBoot: false`.
